NOTICE UNDER SECTION 106 OF THE TRANSFER OF PROPERTY ACT, 1882 FOR DEFAULT IN PAYMENT OF RENT AND TERMINATION OF TENANCY

Sir,

Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, Mrs. SUNANDA VASANT GOKHALE, aged 67 years, residing at 6, Prabhat Road, Lane No. 4, Pune 411004, the absolute owner and landlord of the premises described below, I hereby give you this notice as follows:

1. That my client is the owner and landlord of Shop No. 3, admeasuring 640 square feet, on the Ground Floor of the building known as "Shivaji Chambers", Fergusson College Road, Pune 411004 (the "Premises"), and you are in occupation of the Premises as a monthly tenant of my client under a lease deed dated 3 February 2023 on a monthly rent of Rs 85,000/- (Rupees Eighty-Five Thousand only), exclusive of Goods and Services Tax, payable in advance on or before the 5th day of each English calendar month.

2. That in terms of the said lease deed, the initial period of the tenancy was thirty-six (36) months, and on the expiry of the said period on 31 January 2026 you have continued in possession of the Premises with the consent of my client as a tenant holding over from month to month, on the same terms and conditions, and my client has accepted rent from you in that capacity for the months of February to June 2026.

3. That you have committed default in payment of the monthly rent for the months of July 2026, August 2026 and September 2026, being three (3) consecutive months, and the following amounts are outstanding:

Month              Rent due date     Amount (Rs)
July 2026          5 July 2026       85,000
August 2026        5 August 2026     85,000
September 2026     5 September 2026  85,000
Total arrears                        2,55,000

Rs 2,55,000/- (Rupees Two Lakh Fifty-Five Thousand only) is thus due and payable by you as rent arrears, in addition to the rent for the month of October 2026 which is also due and payable on and from 5 October 2026 and which is not included in the above amount. The security deposit of Rs 5,10,000/- lying with my client cannot be adjusted by you against arrears of rent.

4. That my client has repeatedly requested you, by e-mails dated 8 July 2026, 14 August 2026 and 12 September 2026, and by personal visits, to clear the arrears, but you have not paid the same, and you have on the contrary issued cheques bearing Nos. 004517 and 004518 for Rs 85,000/- each, dated 10 August 2026 and 10 September 2026, drawn on a nationalised bank, which were returned unpaid with the remark "Funds Insufficient". My client reserves the right to initiate proceedings under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 separately, for which a separate notice shall be issued.

5. That your default is wilful, and by reason of your default in payment of rent for more than three (3) months, you are liable to be evicted from the Premises, and you have also committed breach of Clause 7 and Clause 14 of the lease deed regarding payment of rent and subletting, as my client has learnt that you have allowed a third party to use a portion of the Premises for storage of goods.

6. That I, on behalf of my client, hereby call upon you to pay the arrears of rent of Rs 2,55,000/- along with interest at 12% per annum from the respective due dates, as provided in the lease deed, and the rent for October 2026 of Rs 85,000/-, within fifteen (15) days of the receipt of this notice, that is, on or before 4 November 2026, failing which you shall be liable to hand over vacant and peaceful possession of the Premises.

7. That, in the alternative, and without prejudice to the foregoing, this notice also operates as a notice under Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 terminating your tenancy with effect from the midnight of 30 November 2026, being the last day of the month of the tenancy next following the expiry of fifteen (15) days from the date of service of this notice, and you are hereby called upon to quit, vacate and deliver peaceful and vacant possession of the Premises to my client on or before 30 November 2026, and to pay all outstanding rent and damages up to the date of delivery.

8. That if you fail to pay the arrears or to vacate the Premises within the time stated above, my client shall be constrained to institute appropriate proceedings against you in the Court of Small Causes at Pune for recovery of possession and arrears of rent and mesne profits, as well as for damages at the rate of Rs 2,500/- per day for unauthorised occupation, at your risk as to costs and consequences, which you will be liable to bear.

9. That you shall also remove the unauthorised sub-occupant and the stored goods, and pay the notice cost of Rs 7,500/-. This notice is without prejudice to the other rights of my client under the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 and the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, all of which are reserved.

Kindly treat this as a notice under the law and comply within the stipulated time.

Yours faithfully,

(S. P. Kulkarni)
Advocate for Mrs. Sunanda Vasant Gokhale
Enrolment No. MAH/1234/2001

Copy to: Mrs. Sunanda Vasant Gokhale (my client), for information.
